message:
T-2388: the second fort's blockhouse gets the cupola its pictures draw

Panel 5 of the Kurz & Allison sheet — "Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835" — draws a
small square cupola at the centre of this blockhouse's four-sided cap, under a
little cap of its own, and draws no stack anywhere on that roof. The two Wau-Bun
reproductions of the 1831 view draw the same body. Build it, and record the
invented, unattested centre chimney that stood in exactly its place at a count
of 0.

That count is a choice about what to DEPICT and the record says so: it is not a
finding that the blockhouse was unheated, that it had no flue, or that nothing
else stood on that roof. Pictorial silence at tier 5 is not testimony, and the
1856 Kellogg/Blanchard print (filed misleadingly as
chicago_fort_dearborn_river_mouth_1830.jpg) depicts about 1836-1849 and does
show a louvred cap and an ambiguous projection beside it — left unresolved, not
backdated.

The control is a keyword-only, default-off `cupola` on fort_structure, consumed
by a local `_cupola` helper. It is NOT the lighthouse's `lantern` (only _tower
reads that, so setting it here would add nothing), it does not route this
building through the tower builder, and it changes no shared geometry. Validation
accepts only the combination that is built — a blockhouse, a pyramid cap, no
separately generated centre stack — and bounds every dimension. The body is sunk
0.12 m below the lowest the main roof reaches under its own footprint, so it
meets all four sloping planes instead of balancing on the apex: no floating
corner, no strip of sky, nowhere to hide a stack.

Occurrence is inferred from the identified pictures; every dimension is
reconstructed in the archetype and admitted in docs/LIBERTIES.md
L-second-fort-blockhouse-cupola-2388. Everything below the roof is untouched —
surveyed seat and 8 degree rotation, the inferred 14.52 x 9.80 m footprint and
its ambiguity, 5.2 m walls, two storeys, 0.45 m jetty, loopholes, doors, palettes.

Changing the producer staled the family, so all 25 current fort_structure
MASTERs — the accepted 1832 lighthouse and the Lake House shell included — were
genuinely rebuilt on the pinned Ubuntu 26.04 / Blender 4.5.3 in two bounded
native batches. All 25 input hashes in assets/manifest.json are the regenerated
ones; exactly one master's bytes moved (134,632 -> 133,092) and its WEB
derivative was re-encoded, while the other 24 came back byte-identical and keep
their bound derivatives. No foreign registry row touched.

The picture is now on the building's card: the record cites kurz_allison_1893,
and data/structure_grades.json carries an explicit pictured ruling saying why
panel 5 is a reasonable whole picture of this named building — so the sidecar
grade derives `attested` from the rule rather than from a camera fit or a typed
value.

Before and after were captured through photo_match.mjs from one identical
camera with only the blockhouse's bytes changed, in
docs/RESEARCH/second-fort-cupola-T-2388/. The T-3040 bodies are preserved
untouched and the new camera is diagnostic_only. Only the roof assembly is
marked fixed; the view's verdict stays `differs` and T-2388 stays OPEN on the
camera's own fit, the ranges and galleries, the facade openings, the other roof
forms and chimney counts, the compound's composition and every other dated
picture it lists.

Gate: tools/check.sh --part 1/4 through 4/4, all four PASS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

body:
## Verification — all in the foreground, on the exact committed head `f447b68`

### Source gate — all four parts PASS

| part | result |
|---|---|
| `tools/check.sh --part 1/4` | **PASS** — 287 steps, none red |
| `tools/check.sh --part 2/4` | **PASS** — 287 steps, none red |
| `tools/check.sh --part 3/4` | **PASS** — 288 steps, none red |
| `tools/check.sh --part 4/4` | **PASS** — 286 steps, none red |

Part 1 came back red once, on *Source-use backlinks match authored claims (T-1248)* — the
`kurz_allison_1893` edit wanted `tools/compile_source_use.py` re-run. Rebuilt and re-run green.
**No gate step reported a missing module**, so no step here is standing on a banked reading.

### Smoke — both viewports, published mirror, zero page errors

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| `SMOKE_VIEWPORT=desktop SMOKE_STAGE=3` | **SMOKE PASS** — 107 passed, 0 failed, zero page errors, 7 m 01 s |
| `SMOKE_VIEWPORT=mobile SMOKE_STAGE=3-4` | **SMOKE PASS** — 139 passed, 0 failed, zero page errors, 7 m 22 s |

`tools/smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff` names parts **1-15**, because a structure record and
`assets/manifest.json` changed and nothing in those can rule a part out — that is the whole
gate, not a reading of this diff. Part 3 is the one that actually covers what changed here
(*the record's own account, on the card*; *the citation → its document*; the liberties). Two
legs, both well inside the 600 s ceiling, both filed with `tools/dev-smoke-state.mjs record`.
**The whole 15-part gate was not run and is not claimed.**

### The 25-master family, genuinely rebuilt before the first source commit

Two bounded native batches on pinned **Ubuntu 26.04.1 / Blender 4.5.3** (sha256-verified from
`generators/blender.pin`). All 25 `inputs_sha256` in `assets/manifest.json` are the regenerated
ones. **Exactly one master's bytes moved** — `fort_dearborn_blockhouse__log_1816.glb`,
134,632 → 133,092 B, `4b49f0db…` → `96d9fb80…`, WEB derivative re-encoded 29,564 → 28,388 B.
The other 24 came back byte-identical and keep their bound derivatives. No foreign registry row
touched; the independent Jail/`frame_dwelling_271` and first-fort NE/`outbuilding_243` jobs were
left entirely alone.

### Pixels, actually looked at

Published mirror, default 1835 entry, **desktop 1280×800 and phone 390×780**, both:

* **The cupola stands at the apex and MEETS the roof** — its body comes up cleanly through all
  four planes, with no floating corner, no strip of sky and no stack hiding under it, under its
  own overhanging four-sided cap. Jetty, log courses, loopholes and openings below are
  unchanged.
* Confidence view → **By grade** renders it with the rest of the building.
* The card reads **"Attested. Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it."** The **Images**
  tab carries 2 credited public-domain pictures — the Wentworth 1881 keyed reproduction of the
  1831 Wau-Bun view, and the Kurz & Allison 1893 sheet — each with repository, date and rights,
  link-only, no new held media. The **Evidence** tab lists `cupola` among the 7 `inferred`
  claims, reasoned from Kurz & Allison among others. **Record** pane and dossier link present.

Shots, logs, the review script and the full checkpoint:
**[chicago-evidence/evidence/second-fort-2026-11-03/native-blockhouse-cupola-shipped-t2388](https://github.com/kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence/blob/fff86d87b8bb17be2b6aaf782fa0416b8d56d739/evidence/second-fort-2026-11-03/native-blockhouse-cupola-shipped-t2388/RECOVERY.md)**

### What this does not settle

The compound view's verdict stays **`differs`** and **T-2388 is released OPEN**. Only the roof
assembly is marked `fixed`. The camera is the T-3040 landmark fit, reused unchanged so the
before and after differ by geometry alone; it reached its imposed 100 m eye bound, renders the
compound aerial and undersized, and is marked `diagnostic_only`. Still open: that camera's own
fit, the galleried range's identity, the facade openings, the other roof forms and chimney
counts, the compound's composition, and every other dated picture the ticket lists.

issue.title: T-2388: the second fort's blockhouse gets the cupola its pictures draw
issue.body:
## What

The second Fort Dearborn's blockhouse gets the cupola its own pictures draw, and loses the
invented chimney that was standing in its place. **This is a bounded partial increment of
T-2388** — the ticket's all-buildings, all-pictures acceptance is NOT met and the ticket is
released OPEN with the remaining differences recorded.

Panel 5 of the Kurz & Allison sheet of 1893, captioned "Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835", draws
this blockhouse with a small square body at the centre of its four-sided cap, under a little
four-sided cap of its own, and draws no stack anywhere on that roof. The two Wau-Bun
reproductions of the 1831 view (`kinzie_1857_chicago_1831_panorama`) draw the same body. That is
what is now built.

| | |
|---|---|
| before | the invented brick stack at the apex |
| after | the pictured cupola, seated into all four roof planes |

`docs/RESEARCH/second-fort-cupola-T-2388/` holds both, rendered through `photo_match.mjs` from
**one identical camera** with nothing changed between them but the blockhouse's own bytes
(`4b49f0db…` → `96d9fb80…`), beside the panel itself.

## Why, and what is and is not claimed

* **The cupola's OCCURRENCE is inferred** from the two identified pictures. Every dimension —
  the 1.8 m side, the 2.1 m body, the 0.22 m cap eave, the 36° cap pitch, the 0.12 m seat, the
  plain boarded sides with no louvres and no finial — is **reconstructed**, lives in the
  archetype rather than the record, and is admitted in `docs/LIBERTIES.md`
  § `L-second-fort-blockhouse-cupola-2388`. A tier-5 retrospective chromolithograph supplies
  form, never a metric, and its caption is not proof the feature stood on 1 July 1835.
* **`chimneys: 0` is a choice about what to DEPICT, not a finding about heating.**
  `_chimneys` stands its single stack at exactly the centre of the plan — the cupola's place —
  so the two could not both be built and one of them is pictured. The record says in as many
  words that this is not a claim of no heating, no flue, or no later secondary projection, and
  the stack has not been quietly moved somewhere else. The 1856 Kellogg/Blanchard print (filed
  misleadingly as `chicago_fort_dearborn_river_mouth_1830.jpg`) depicts about 1836–1849 and does
  show a louvred cap and an ambiguous projection beside it; that later detail is left
  unresolved, not backdated.
* **The join is real.** A box set down at the apex floats clear of the covering at its own
  corners, because the pyramid falls away in every direction — a strip of sky, and somewhere to
  hide a stack. The body's foot is carried 0.12 m below the lowest the main roof reaches
  anywhere under its footprint, so it comes up through all four planes. The main roof is the
  same four planes `_hip_roof` has always laid.

## How

* `fort_structure_params.py`: a keyword-only, **default-off** `cupola` field (added to
  `CONSUMED`, read by `from_phase`), its five reconstructed dimensions as named module
  constants, and validation that accepts **only the combination that is built** — a
  `blockhouse`, a `pyramid` roof, and no separately generated centre stack — with every
  dimension bounded and checked finite. Existing records and callers keep exactly their previous
  semantics; nothing is turned on globally.
* `fort_structure.py`: a local `_cupola` helper, called from `_building` only when the record
  asks. **Not** the lighthouse's `lantern` (only `_tower` consumes that, so setting it on a
  blockhouse would add nothing at all), not routed through the tower builder, no shared geometry
  changed. `_hip_roof`'s own overhang is now a named constant so `_cupola` reads it instead of
  copying the literal.
* `data/structures/fort_dearborn_blockhouse.json`: `form.cupola` (inferred, with its sources and
  reasoning), `form.chimneys` 1 → 0 with the full admission, and the `roof_type` note corrected —
  it used to end "no cupola is built here".
* The record keeps the `fort_structure(kind=blockhouse)` / `log_1816` phase, the surveyed seat
  and 8° rotation, the inferred 14.52 × 9.80 m footprint **and its ±25 % ambiguity**, the 5.2 m
  reconstructed walls, two storeys, the 0.45 m jetty, loopholes, doors, main pyramid at 30° and
  every palette.

## The 25-master family

Changing the producer stales every `fort_structure` asset, so **all 25 current masters** — the
already accepted 1832 lighthouse and the Lake House construction shell included — were genuinely
rebuilt on pinned **Ubuntu 26.04 / Blender 4.5.3** in two bounded native batches before the first
source commit. All 25 `inputs_sha256` in `assets/manifest.json` are the regenerated ones.
**Exactly one master's bytes moved** — `fort_dearborn_blockhouse__log_1816.glb`,
134,632 → 133,092 — and its WEB derivative was re-encoded; the other 24 came back
byte-identical and keep their genuinely bound existing derivatives. No foreign registry row was
touched, and no other job's source, claims or branches were gone near.

## The picture on the card

`kurz_allison_1893` is cited by the record, which is what puts it on the Images tab through
`compile_pictures.py`. `data/structure_grades.json` carries an explicit **pictured ruling**
saying why panel 5 is a reasonable whole picture of this named building, so the sidecar grade
derives `attested` from the rule — not hand-typed, and **not** taken as a camera-fit shortcut:
the only camera on this panel is the T-3040 compound diagnostic, whose eye reached its imposed
100 m bound, and the ruling says so.

## Verification

* `tools/check.sh --part 1/4`, `2/4`, `3/4`, `4/4` — **all four PASS**, every one a bounded
  foreground run (part 1 re-run after `compile_source_use.py` rebuilt its backlinks). No gate
  step reported a missing module.
* `tools/compile_liberties.py`, `tools/compile_scene.py --all`, `tools/compile_source_use.py`,
  `tools/changelog-entries.mjs --check`, `tools/publish.sh` — all clean.
* Before/after compound comparison through `photo_match.mjs`, same camera, both committed.
* Smoke: the parts `tools/smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff` names for this diff, at **1280×800 and
  390×780**, reported in a comment below.

## What is NOT claimed

The view's verdict is **`differs`** and `T-2388` is **released OPEN**. Still open on this
building's own picture: the camera is an unfitted 100 m diagnostic and is marked
`diagnostic_only`; the galleried range's identity, the facade openings, the other roof forms and
chimney counts, and the compound's whole composition are unresolved; and the other dated
pictures the ticket lists have not been read against the model at all. Only the roof assembly is
marked `fixed`. No new photo ticket, no split, no `done --pr`.
